title: A Kidney Drug May Help Millions More
hook: Three major studies found finerenone protects the kidneys and heart in far more people than thought — including those with non-diabetic kidney disease, a group with few good options.
key_points: A trio of major studies found finerenone slowed kidney disease and cut risks of kidney failure, heart failure, and cardiovascular death.
Benefits showed up not just in people with diabetes but in non-diabetic kidney disease too.
Non-diabetic kidney disease has had limited treatment options — this widens them.
Chronic kidney disease is common and often silent, so a broadly effective drug matters.
content_html: Finerenone, a drug already used for kidney disease in people with diabetes, may help far more patients than doctors realized. A trio of major studies found it slowed kidney disease progression and reduced the risks of kidney failure, heart failure, cardiovascular death, and death from any cause.
extra_html: The striking part: benefits appeared not only in patients with diabetes but also in those with non-diabetic kidney disease — a group that has had limited treatment options. Because chronic kidney disease is common and often silent until late, a drug that protects both kidneys and heart across more patients is a meaningful expansion. Reported by ScienceDaily.

related.title: The Silent Spread of Kidney Disease
related.hook: A global study estimates chronic kidney disease now affects nearly 800 million people — often silently — making it a leading and frequently overlooked cause of death.

related.title: Keeping Your Heart Healthy
related.hook: Most heart disease isn't bad luck — it's the sum of a few everyday habits. The American Heart Association distills them into eight that move the needle most.

flashcards.explanation_html: Finerenone was already used in diabetic kidney disease; the new studies found benefits in non-diabetic kidney disease as well — a group with limited options.

flashcards.prompt: Beyond the kidneys, what else did finerenone appear to protect?
flashcards.back_html: The heart — the studies found reduced risks of heart failure, cardiovascular death, and death from any cause, alongside slower kidney disease progression.

flashcards.prompt: Why does extending finerenone to non-diabetic kidney disease matter so much?
flashcards.back_html: That group has had limited treatment options, and chronic kidney disease is common and often silent until late — so a broadly protective drug fills a real gap.
